_comment: Model-assignment heuristics for this repository (Sprint 4 Task K, F18, 2026-09-19). Data-driven complement to the static role table in docs/SPRINT_PLANNING.md: which model tier AND which review protocol a task pattern gets, with the outcomes that justify it. Modeled on spamfilter-multi's .claude/model_assignment_heuristics.json (read-only survey, Sprint 3 Task A), rewritten for this repository. Every number in learning_log names its source document; a success_rate is null until sample_size is at least 1 real outcome, never estimated. Update at every retrospective (Category 5, Model Assignments) and whenever a delegated task's report is verified against repository state. Guarded by tests/test_model_assignment_heuristics.py.

opus.role: Lead Developer when Fable is unavailable

fable.role: Lead Developer, top tier (mandatory for planning, retrospectives, refinement, ADR authoring, schema and context decisions, security-sensitive review)

team_lead.role: Adjudication of record verdicts; merges at every level; every Class 1/2/3 decision
team_lead.source: docs/SPRINT_PROCESS.md; ADR-0005 section 2c (read tier: 'Team lead, real')

protocols._comment: Protocol is a first-class field beside tier. Sprint 3's F7-F10 result on the identical 18 records: the two protocols that required cross-record comparison or primary-source verification found the defects; the two per-record internal-consistency protocols confirmed 18/18. Review depth tracked the protocol at least as much as the tier (SPRINT_3_RETROSPECTIVE.md improvement 4). A review card names its protocol explicitly regardless of the tier assigned.

per-record-internal-consistency.description: Confirm or reject each record against its own fields, quoting an exact anchor per confirmation. Detects internal contradictions; does not detect a citation that is wrong on the source.

per-record-with-certainty-check.description: per-record-internal-consistency plus a check that certainty_reasons justify the assigned certainty on any yielded assertion; declares the step not applicable when there are no yields.

set-level-cross-record.description: Review the records as a SET: find the same judgment made differently across records with no stated reason (pairwise comparisons within thematic clusters plus whole-set sweeps).

full-adjudication-primary-source.description: ACCEPT/REJECT/REVISE every field on every record, verified against primary sources (arXiv abstract pages, publisher pages, local PDFs read directly).

team-lead-adjudication.description: The team lead adjudicates the corrected records with the same primary-source access the full-adjudication protocol used, recording minutes per record and the protocol actually followed per record (F11).

task_patterns.rationale: On 18 identical records the protocol, not the tier alone, produced the findings; a card that assigns a lower tier must still require cross-record comparison and primary-source verification.

task_patterns.pattern: hook or guard implementation with subprocess tests
task_patterns.required_protocol: injection-proof (break, watch red, restore; recorded in the docstring)
task_patterns.rationale: docs/SPRINT_PLANNING.md: implementation tasks may be delegated; docs/TESTING_STRATEGY.md: every guard proven to fail. Fable review of the delegated report against repository state before it is trusted.
task_patterns.source: SPRINT_4_PLAN.md Task I assignment (outcome to be recorded at the Sprint 4 retrospective)

task_patterns.pattern: process design, ADR amendment, schema or context decision
task_patterns.required_protocol: verify before amending; dated amendment, never an edit in place; Class 1 surfaced to the team lead
task_patterns.rationale: Mandatory top tier per docs/SPRINT_PLANNING.md; touches an ACCEPTED ADR's spine.

task_patterns.pattern: read-only survey of a sibling repository
task_patterns.required_protocol: read-only (hook-enforced by block_sibling_repo_writes.py); report verified against repository state before trusted or dismissed
task_patterns.rationale: Sprint 3 Task A: a fork carried the reading (266 s, 433,817 tokens) and its accurate report was briefly distrusted after a context compaction; the fix was git show, not a judgment about the messenger (SPRINT_3_RETROSPECTIVE.md improvement 3).

task_patterns.pattern: documentation-only edit with no scope ambiguity
task_patterns.required_protocol: run tests/test_no_em_dashes.py and tests/test_us_english.py before commit
task_patterns.rationale: Lowest-effort pattern; the two prose guards catch the two failure modes this repository has actually paid for.
task_patterns.source: SPRINT_4_PLAN.md Task J assignment (Haiku or Sonnet)

escalation_triggers.trigger: a delegated task's report claims a commit, a file, or a closed issue that repository state does not show
escalation_triggers.action: do not re-delegate; verify with git show and the file, then escalate one tier only if the discrepancy is in the work rather than in the report

escalation_triggers.trigger: a review card at any tier confirms every record with zero rejections
escalation_triggers.action: treat as evidence the protocol lacked primary-source access, not as evidence the records are correct; re-run with full-adjudication-primary-source before acting on the confirmation

escalation_triggers.trigger: a guard test passes on first write without an injection
escalation_triggers.action: break the guarded thing before trusting it (CLAUDE.md); a subagent that reports green without naming what it broke is asked for the injection, not believed

escalation_triggers.trigger: a task's true size reaches 2x its estimate
escalation_triggers.action: Criterion 3 stop: present original vs new estimate; never defer approved work unilaterally

escalation_triggers.trigger: the decision touches an ACCEPTED ADR's spine, a certainty level, or approved scope
escalation_triggers.action: Class 1/2/3: stop and surface to the team lead as a plain numbered list

scoring_rubric._comment: Additive score, then a tier threshold. Deliberately coarse until sample sizes exist; the protocol field above, not this score, is what the F7-F10 evidence actually supports.

thresholds.team_lead: any record verdict, every merge, every Class 1/2/3 decision

learning_log.task: F7-F10 independent adjudication review of the same 18 screened-tier paper records, zero cross-visibility

outcomes.findings: 18/18 confirm; correctly declared the certainty step not applicable (zero yields)
93 field calls: 38 accept / 43 revise / 12 reject; 4 source-verified citation defects; 2 structural findings

learning_log.lesson: The heuristic this seeds is NOT 'use the top tier': the protocol (cross-record comparison, primary-source verification) produced the findings, and any review card must require that protocol explicitly regardless of the tier assigned. Every defect the Fable-tier review found sits inside records the Haiku-tier review confirmed.

learning_log.task: F11 team-lead adjudication timing on the 18 records as corrected by Sprint 4 Task C, F10 protocol, same primary-source access
learning_log.source: SPRINT_4_PLAN.md Task E; packet delivered 2026-09-19 as docs/sprints/SPRINT_4_F11_ADJUDICATION_PACKET.md (generated by scripts/render_f11_packet.py); the row is filled in when the team lead's timing lands, never estimated

outcomes.findings: 18/18 accept, 0 revise, 0 reject on the records as corrected by Tasks C, F and H
outcomes.protocol_followed_per_record: full (team lead's answer on each of 18; the interval per record ran from the moment the record was shown to the moment the answer arrived, so it includes reading the packet entry and opening the source link, and about 20-40 s of Claude's presentation latency per record)
outcomes.run: interactive, one record per turn, 2026-09-21 22:33 to 22:52 local; log docs/sprints/SPRINT_4_F11_TIMING_LOG.json

learning_log.lesson: The number ADR-0004 is constrained by, first measurement: about 1.1 team-lead minutes per record (19.4 min for 18) to adjudicate records that a model pipeline had already corrected (API-derived citations, anchored rationales, F10's finding printed under each). Against F10's 599 s of model time for the same 18 (33 s per record), the team lead spent about twice the wall clock and confirmed everything. Two readings, both recorded: (1) the corrections held on a second, human pass; (2) by this file's own escalation trigger, a run that confirms every record with zero rejections is evidence about the protocol's depth as much as about the records -- the team lead answered 'full' per record, but the protocol here was confirm-mode over pre-corrected records with the finding in view, not the cold primary-source adjudication F10 ran. The cost that matters for scale is therefore: confirm-mode team-lead review of model-corrected records is about a minute per record; cold adjudication was not measured and remains the open number.
